title: Appeal of Te Sung Keon Kim vs. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained on procedural grounds: the SJC answered no to whether the judicial commission followed BCO procedures and remanded the case to Presbytery for a new trial in compliance with BCO 32 and 34. The SJC did not rule on the merits, the adequacy of the citations, or whether a default judgment without hearing, testimony, or minutes is proper.
first_summary: A minister appealed his five-year suspension after a default heresy/schism judgment. The SJC held that the judicial commission failed BCO 32 and 34 because no indictment was served and no hearing record existed, reversed the suspension, and remanded for a new trial in compliance with those provisions.
summary: A minister suspended for five years after a default judgment of heresy and schism appealed to the SJC. The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, holding the judicial commission did not follow BCO 32 and 34: no indictment was served, and the record lacked minutes or evidence of a hearing. It remanded to Korean Capital Presbytery for a new trial. The SJC expressly did not reach the merits, the adequacy of the citations, or whether default judgment is proper.
